---- MODULE W4Od5m4p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, QueueBound, PoolSize, MaxEpoch

ASSUME /\ QueueBound \in Nat /\ QueueBound > 0
       /\ PoolSize \in Nat /\ PoolSize > 0
       /\ MaxEpoch \in Nat /\ MaxEpoch > 0

VARIABLES sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ, casualQ, busyServers

vars == <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ, casualQ, busyServers>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ sessionEpoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ stampedAt \in [Players -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
  /\ rankedQ \subseteq Players
  /\ casualQ \subseteq Players
  /\ busyServers \in 0 .. PoolSize

Waiting == rankedQ \cup casualQ

QueuedTicketsAreCurrentAndUnique ==
  /\ \A p \in Waiting : stampedAt[p] = sessionEpoch
  /\ rankedQ \cap casualQ = {}

Init ==
  /\ sessionEpoch = 0
  /\ stampedAt = [p \in Players |-> 0]
  /\ rankedQ = {}
  /\ casualQ = {}
  /\ busyServers = 0

RotateEpoch ==
  /\ sessionEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ sessionEpoch' = sessionEpoch + 1
  /\ rankedQ' = {}
  /\ casualQ' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stampedAt, busyServers>>

RefreshToken(p) ==
  /\ stampedAt[p] < sessionEpoch
  /\ stampedAt' = [stampedAt EXCEPT ![p] = sessionEpoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, rankedQ, casualQ, busyServers>>

AdmitRanked(p) ==
  /\ stampedAt[p] = sessionEpoch
  /\ p \notin Waiting
  /\ Cardinality(rankedQ) < QueueBound
  /\ rankedQ' = rankedQ \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, casualQ, busyServers>>

AdmitCasual(p) ==
  /\ stampedAt[p] = sessionEpoch
  /\ p \notin Waiting
  /\ Cardinality(casualQ) < QueueBound
  /\ casualQ' = casualQ \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ, busyServers>>

StartRankedMatch(p) ==
  /\ p \in rankedQ
  /\ busyServers < PoolSize
  /\ rankedQ' = rankedQ \ {p}
  /\ busyServers' = busyServers + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, casualQ>>

StartCasualMatch(p) ==
  /\ p \in casualQ
  /\ busyServers < PoolSize
  /\ casualQ' = casualQ \ {p}
  /\ busyServers' = busyServers + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ>>

MatchFinishes ==
  /\ busyServers > 0
  /\ busyServers' = busyServers - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionEpoch, stampedAt, rankedQ, casualQ>>

Next ==
  \/ RotateEpoch \/ MatchFinishes
  \/ \E p \in Players :
       \/ RefreshToken(p) \/ AdmitRanked(p) \/ AdmitCasual(p)
       \/ StartRankedMatch(p) \/ StartCasualMatch(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
    Players = {plrA, plrB}
    QueueBound = 1
    PoolSize = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT QueuedTicketsAreCurrentAndUnique
nl:
A game studio runs two matchmakers side by side: the ranked matchmaker and the casual matchmaker. They were written by different teams, ship on different cadences, and know nothing about each other. What they share is one pool of game servers, and a server running a ranked match is a server that cannot run a casual one.

Each matchmaker keeps its own waiting queue, and each queue is bounded. When a queue is at its bound the matchmaker applies backpressure: it simply refuses to take another ticket until a match starts and a place frees up. The bound is what stops a queue growing without limit during an outage and then dumping thousands of stale tickets onto the pool when the outage clears.

Tickets are only as good as the session they were minted in. The account service stamps a session epoch on every player token, and rotates the epoch when it rolls a new authentication key -- after a credential leak, after a client patch, at the start of a season. A token stamped with an older epoch is stale, and a stale token is not a player the matchmakers may act on. Rotating the epoch therefore empties both waiting queues in the same motion, because everything sitting in them was admitted on the strength of a token that no longer means anything. A player whose token has gone stale refreshes it against the current epoch and can then queue again.

The one thing neither matchmaker can check for itself is whether the other has already taken a player, so the studio enforces it at the point of admission: a player is only admitted to a queue if they are in neither queue at that moment.

The actions of the system are: the account service rotating the session epoch and emptying both queues, a player refreshing a stale token against the current epoch, admitting a current-token player who is in neither queue to the ranked queue while it is under its bound, admitting such a player to the casual queue while it is under its bound, starting a ranked match on a free server and taking that player off the ranked queue, starting a casual match on a free server and taking that player off the casual queue, and a match finishing and releasing its server.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every player sitting in either waiting queue holds a token stamped with the current session epoch, and no player is in both queues at once.

---- MODULE W4Od14m4p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS DroneOne, DroneTwo, QueueBound, MaxPreempts, NoDrone

Drones == {DroneOne, DroneTwo}

ASSUME /\ DroneOne # DroneTwo
       /\ NoDrone \notin Drones
       /\ QueueBound \in Nat /\ QueueBound > 0
       /\ MaxPreempts \in Nat

VARIABLES uplink, sending, buffered, asking, preemptsLeft

vars == <<uplink, sending, buffered, asking, preemptsLeft>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ uplink \in Drones \cup {NoDrone}
  /\ sending \subseteq Drones
  /\ buffered \in [Drones -> 0 .. QueueBound]
  /\ asking \subseteq Drones
  /\ preemptsLeft \in 0 .. MaxPreempts

OnlyTheUplinkHolderTransmits ==
  /\ sending \subseteq {uplink}
  /\ \A d \in sending : buffered[d] > 0

Init ==
  /\ uplink = NoDrone
  /\ sending = {}
  /\ buffered = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ asking = {}
  /\ preemptsLeft = MaxPreempts

BufferFrame(d) ==
  /\ buffered[d] < QueueBound
  /\ buffered' = [buffered EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<uplink, sending, asking, preemptsLeft>>

AskForUplink(d) ==
  /\ buffered[d] > 0
  /\ d \notin asking
  /\ asking' = asking \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<uplink, sending, buffered, preemptsLeft>>

GrantUplink(d) ==
  /\ uplink = NoDrone
  /\ d \in asking
  /\ uplink' = d
  /\ asking' = asking \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sending, buffered, preemptsLeft>>

KeyTransmitter(d) ==
  /\ uplink = d
  /\ d \notin sending
  /\ buffered[d] > 0
  /\ sending' = sending \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<uplink, buffered, asking, preemptsLeft>>

DrainFrame(d) ==
  /\ d \in sending
  /\ buffered[d] > 1
  /\ buffered' = [buffered EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<uplink, sending, asking, preemptsLeft>>

StopAndRelease(d) ==
  /\ uplink = d
  /\ sending' = sending \ {d}
  /\ uplink' = NoDrone
  /\ UNCHANGED <<buffered, asking, preemptsLeft>>

CommanderPreempts(d) ==
  /\ preemptsLeft > 0
  /\ uplink # NoDrone
  /\ uplink # d
  /\ uplink' = d
  /\ sending' = {}
  /\ asking' = asking \ {d}
  /\ preemptsLeft' = preemptsLeft - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED buffered

Next ==
  \E d \in Drones :
    \/ BufferFrame(d) \/ AskForUplink(d) \/ GrantUplink(d)
    \/ KeyTransmitter(d) \/ DrainFrame(d) \/ StopAndRelease(d)
    \/ CommanderPreempts(d)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(StopAndRelease(DroneOne))
  /\ WF_vars(StopAndRelease(DroneTwo))

TransmissionsAlwaysEnd ==
  \A d \in Drones : (d \in sending) ~> (d \notin sending)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    DroneOne = droneOne
    DroneTwo = droneTwo
    QueueBound = 2
    MaxPreempts = 1
    NoDrone = noDrone
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheUplinkHolderTransmits
PROPERTY TransmissionsAlwaysEnd
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm carries one satellite uplink between all of its drones. The uplink is a single radio: two drones keying it at the same time produce a collision that costs the ground station the whole pass, so exactly one drone may be transmitting at any instant, and only the drone that currently holds the uplink may transmit at all.

Imagery comes off the sensors faster than the uplink can carry it, so each drone buffers frames into a bounded outbound queue. When a drone's queue is full it applies backpressure and stops accepting frames from its own sensor rather than overwriting what is already buffered -- a dropped frame in the middle of a burn perimeter is worse than a gap at the end of it. A drone with nothing buffered has no reason to want the uplink; a drone with frames buffered asks for it and waits its turn.

Holding the uplink is a three-step affair: a waiting drone is granted the uplink, keys the transmitter and starts sending, and then stops sending and gives the uplink back when its buffer has drained enough. The grant is what makes the exclusion work: a drone that has not been granted the uplink never keys the transmitter.

The incident commander can preempt. When a spotter drone has line of sight on a new head of fire, the commander takes the uplink away from whoever has it -- stopping that drone's transmission in the same motion -- and gives it to the drone that matters. Preemption is rationed for the flight, because every preemption is a truncated frame somebody has to re-fly.

The actions of the system are: a drone buffering a frame from its own sensor while its queue is under its bound, a drone with frames buffered asking for the uplink, granting the uplink to a waiting drone, the holder keying the transmitter and starting to send, the holder stopping and giving the uplink back, a drone draining one frame out of its buffer while transmitting, and the incident commander preempting the uplink away from whoever holds it and stopping that drone's transmission.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of drones transmitting is always contained in the set containing just the drone that currently holds the uplink, so two drones never key the radio at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A drone that has started transmitting eventually stops transmitting, whether it finishes on its own or the incident commander preempts it.

---- MODULE W4Od13m0p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drivers, Columns, MaxFacings, MaxGen, NoColumn

ASSUME /\ NoColumn \notin Columns
       /\ MaxFacings \in Nat /\ MaxFacings > 0
       /\ MaxGen \in Nat /\ MaxGen > 0

VARIABLES stock, facings, planGen, claimOn, notedGen

vars == <<stock, facings, planGen, claimOn, notedGen>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ stock \in [Columns -> 0 .. MaxFacings]
  /\ facings \in [Columns -> 1 .. MaxFacings]
  /\ planGen \in 0 .. MaxGen
  /\ claimOn \in [Drivers -> Columns \cup {NoColumn}]
  /\ notedGen \in [Drivers -> 0 .. MaxGen]

Claiming == {d \in Drivers : claimOn[d] # NoColumn}

StockFitsTheFacings ==
  /\ \A c \in Columns : stock[c] <= facings[c]
  /\ \A d \in Claiming : notedGen[d] <= planGen

Init ==
  /\ stock = [c \in Columns |-> 0]
  /\ facings = [c \in Columns |-> MaxFacings]
  /\ planGen = 0
  /\ claimOn = [d \in Drivers |-> NoColumn]
  /\ notedGen = [d \in Drivers |-> 0]

OpenClaim(d, c) ==
  /\ claimOn[d] = NoColumn
  /\ claimOn' = [claimOn EXCEPT ![d] = c]
  /\ notedGen' = [notedGen EXCEPT ![d] = planGen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, facings, planGen>>

Restock(d) ==
  /\ claimOn[d] # NoColumn
  /\ notedGen[d] = planGen
  /\ stock[claimOn[d]] < facings[claimOn[d]]
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![claimOn[d]] = @ + 1]
  /\ claimOn' = [claimOn EXCEPT ![d] = NoColumn]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<facings, planGen, notedGen>>

AbandonStale(d) ==
  /\ claimOn[d] # NoColumn
  /\ notedGen[d] # planGen
  /\ claimOn' = [claimOn EXCEPT ![d] = NoColumn]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, facings, planGen, notedGen>>

AbandonFull(d) ==
  /\ claimOn[d] # NoColumn
  /\ notedGen[d] = planGen
  /\ stock[claimOn[d]] = facings[claimOn[d]]
  /\ claimOn' = [claimOn EXCEPT ![d] = NoColumn]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, facings, planGen, notedGen>>

Republish(f) ==
  /\ planGen < MaxGen
  /\ f \in [Columns -> 1 .. MaxFacings]
  /\ \A c \in Columns : f[c] >= stock[c]
  /\ facings' = f
  /\ planGen' = planGen + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, claimOn, notedGen>>

Purchase(c) ==
  /\ stock[c] > 0
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<facings, planGen, claimOn, notedGen>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in [Columns -> 1 .. MaxFacings] : Republish(f)
  \/ \E c \in Columns : Purchase(c)
  \/ \E d \in Drivers :
       \/ Restock(d) \/ AbandonStale(d) \/ AbandonFull(d)
       \/ \E c \in Columns : OpenClaim(d, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
    Drivers = {routeDrvA, routeDrvB}
    Columns = {colA, colB}
    MaxFacings = 2
    MaxGen = 2
    NoColumn = noColumn
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT StockFitsTheFacings
nl:
A vending operator's machines hold their product in columns, and each column has a number of facings -- how many units of that product physically fit in it. Route drivers restock the columns from handhelds, with no lock anywhere: a driver opens a claim against a column, notes the planogram generation the machine was running when the claim was opened, and restocks only if the machine is still running that generation.

The planogram is the thing that changes underneath them. Head office republishes it during the day as promotions start and finish, and republishing sets new facings for every column at once and advances the generation. Facings can go down as well as up -- a column that was three facings of one drink becomes two of another -- but head office may never publish facings below what a column is already holding, because there is nowhere for displaced units to go and pulling stock back out of a machine is a separate, audited job.

A driver whose claim was opened against an older generation is working from a planogram that no longer applies, and abandons the claim rather than restocking against it. A driver whose claim is current but whose column is already full to its facings also abandons, since there is nothing to put in. Customers buying product take units out of columns and are what makes room again.

The actions of the system are: a driver opening a claim against a column and noting the current planogram generation, a driver restocking one unit into a column whose noted generation still matches and which is under its facings, a driver abandoning a claim whose noted generation no longer matches, a driver abandoning a current claim on a column that is already full to its facings, head office republishing the planogram with new facings no lower than what each column already holds, and a customer buying a unit out of a column.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No column ever holds more units than its current facings, and no driver's open claim was noted against a planogram generation ahead of the one in force.

---- MODULE W4Od12m0p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS TechOne, TechTwo, Units, MaxClock, MaxRev, NoUnit

Techs == {TechOne, TechTwo}

ASSUME /\ TechOne # TechTwo
       /\ NoUnit \notin Units
       /\ MaxClock \in Nat /\ MaxRev \in Nat

VARIABLES auditClock, certTo, postingOn, notedRev, rev

vars == <<auditClock, certTo, postingOn, notedRev, rev>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ auditClock \in 0 .. MaxClock
  /\ certTo \in [Techs -> 0 .. MaxClock]
  /\ postingOn \in [Techs -> Units \cup {NoUnit}]
  /\ notedRev \in [Techs -> 0 .. MaxRev]
  /\ rev \in [Units -> 0 .. MaxRev]

Open == {t \in Techs : postingOn[t] # NoUnit}

OpenPostingsAreCertifiedAndSane ==
  /\ \A t \in Open : certTo[t] >= auditClock
  /\ \A t \in Open : notedRev[t] <= rev[postingOn[t]]

Init ==
  /\ auditClock = 0
  /\ certTo = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
  /\ postingOn = [t \in Techs |-> NoUnit]
  /\ notedRev = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
  /\ rev = [u \in Units |-> 0]

AdvanceClock ==
  /\ auditClock < MaxClock
  /\ auditClock' = auditClock + 1
  /\ postingOn' = [t \in Techs |->
                     IF certTo[t] < auditClock + 1 THEN NoUnit ELSE postingOn[t]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<certTo, notedRev, rev>>

Recertify(t) ==
  /\ certTo[t] < MaxClock
  /\ certTo' = [certTo EXCEPT ![t] = MaxClock]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, postingOn, notedRev, rev>>

OpenPosting(t, u) ==
  /\ certTo[t] >= auditClock
  /\ postingOn[t] = NoUnit
  /\ postingOn' = [postingOn EXCEPT ![t] = u]
  /\ notedRev' = [notedRev EXCEPT ![t] = rev[u]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, certTo, rev>>

WritePosting(t) ==
  /\ certTo[t] >= auditClock
  /\ postingOn[t] # NoUnit
  /\ notedRev[t] = rev[postingOn[t]]
  /\ rev[postingOn[t]] < MaxRev
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![postingOn[t]] = @ + 1]
  /\ postingOn' = [postingOn EXCEPT ![t] = NoUnit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, certTo, notedRev>>

ReRead(t) ==
  /\ postingOn[t] # NoUnit
  /\ notedRev[t] # rev[postingOn[t]]
  /\ notedRev' = [notedRev EXCEPT ![t] = rev[postingOn[t]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, certTo, postingOn, rev>>

CloseAtCeiling(t) ==
  /\ postingOn[t] # NoUnit
  /\ rev[postingOn[t]] = MaxRev
  /\ postingOn' = [postingOn EXCEPT ![t] = NoUnit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<auditClock, certTo, notedRev, rev>>

Clears(t) == WritePosting(t) \/ ReRead(t) \/ CloseAtCeiling(t)

Next ==
  \/ AdvanceClock
  \/ \E t \in Techs :
       \/ Clears(t) \/ Recertify(t)
       \/ \E u \in Units : OpenPosting(t, u)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Clears(TechOne))
  /\ WF_vars(Clears(TechTwo))

OpenPostingsAlwaysClose ==
  \A t \in Techs : (postingOn[t] # NoUnit) ~> (postingOn[t] = NoUnit)

====

CONSTANTS
    TechOne = bankTechOne
    TechTwo = bankTechTwo
    Units = {unitA, unitB}
    MaxClock = 2
    MaxRev = 2
    NoUnit = noUnit
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OpenPostingsAreCertifiedAndSane
PROPERTY OpenPostingsAlwaysClose
nl:
A blood bank's inventory records are posted to by technicians working without any lock on the record. A technician opens a posting against a unit record, notes the revision the record was on, and writes only if the record is still on that revision; if it has moved, the technician re-reads and works from the new revision instead.

Who may post is governed by the competency register. Every technician's competency is certified to a particular point on the bank's audit clock, and the clock advances as the day's audit windows close. A technician whose certification point is behind the clock is out of certification and may not post to anything. The bank is strict about this because a posting made by an uncertified technician has to be backed out by hand and every unit it touched has to be re-tested. When the clock advances past a technician's certification point, any posting that technician had open is closed out in the same motion -- the posting cannot be allowed to sit there and land later. Technicians re-certify against the register and can then post again.

Technicians here are slow, not broken. A technician is interrupted by a cross-match, a phone call from theatre, a courier at the door; a posting can sit open across several clock advances while the record underneath it moves on. That is what the re-read is for, and it is why the certification check has to be made again at the moment of writing rather than only when the posting was opened.

Unit records stop accepting postings once they reach the revision ceiling the bank keeps for a single audit day; a technician holding a posting against a record at the ceiling closes it out rather than re-reading forever.

The actions of the system are: the audit clock advancing and closing out the postings of every technician whose certification is now behind it, a technician re-certifying against the register, a certified technician opening a posting against a unit record and noting its revision, a certified technician writing a posting whose noted revision still matches and advancing the record, a technician re-reading a record whose revision moved underneath its open posting, and a technician closing out a posting against a record that has reached the day's revision ceiling.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every technician with a posting open is certified to a point at or beyond the current audit clock, and no open posting was noted against a revision ahead of the one its record is actually on.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A technician with a posting open eventually has no posting open, whether it is written, closed out at the ceiling, or closed out when the clock passes that technician's certification.

CONSTANTS Nodes, Blocks, MaxTerm, MaxOverrides, NoNode

ASSUME /\ NoNode \notin Nodes
       /\ Blocks \in Nat /\ Blocks > 0
       /\ MaxTerm \in Nat /\ MaxTerm > 0

VARIABLES seat, term, served, shedded, spare, overridesLeft

vars == <<seat, term, served, shedded, spare, overridesLeft>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ seat \in Nodes \cup {NoNode}
  /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
  /\ served \in 0 .. Blocks
  /\ shedded \in 0 .. Blocks
  /\ spare \in 0 .. Blocks
  /\ overridesLeft \in 0 .. MaxOverrides

DemandBlocksAreConserved == served + shedded + spare = Blocks

Init ==
  /\ seat = NoNode
  /\ term = 0
  /\ served = Blocks
  /\ shedded = 0
  /\ spare = 0
  /\ overridesLeft = MaxOverrides

ElectCoordinator(n) ==
  /\ seat = NoNode
  /\ seat' = n
  /\ term' = IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE term
  /\ UNCHANGED <<served, shedded, spare, overridesLeft>>

CoordinatorFalls ==
  /\ seat # NoNode
  /\ seat' = NoNode
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, served, shedded, spare, overridesLeft>>

ShedBlock ==
  /\ seat # NoNode
  /\ served > 0
  /\ served' = served - 1
  /\ shedded' = shedded + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, spare, overridesLeft>>

RestoreBlock ==
  /\ seat # NoNode
  /\ shedded > 0
  /\ shedded' = shedded - 1
  /\ served' = served + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, spare, overridesLeft>>

CommissionSpare ==
  /\ seat # NoNode
  /\ spare > 0
  /\ spare' = spare - 1
  /\ served' = served + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, shedded, overridesLeft>>

TakeForMaintenance ==
  /\ served > 0
  /\ served' = served - 1
  /\ spare' = spare + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, shedded, overridesLeft>>

OperatorOverride ==
  /\ overridesLeft > 0
  /\ served > 0
  /\ served' = served - 1
  /\ shedded' = shedded + 1
  /\ overridesLeft' = overridesLeft - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, term, spare>>

Next ==
  \/ CoordinatorFalls \/ ShedBlock \/ RestoreBlock \/ CommissionSpare
  \/ TakeForMaintenance \/ OperatorOverride
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : ElectCoordinator(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {shedNodeA, shedNodeB}
    Blocks = 3
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxOverrides = 1
    NoNode = noNode
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DemandBlocksAreConserved
nl:
A regional power grid runs an automatic load shedder over a fixed block of demand. The demand is measured in whole blocks and the number of blocks is fixed for the interval: the shedder does not create demand and it does not destroy it, it only moves blocks between three states. A block is either being served, or shed, or held in spare -- capacity that is committed to nothing at this instant and is available to be commissioned into service.

The shedder is driven by one coordinator node at a time. The nodes elect a coordinator and the election stamps a term number on the winner, up to the highest term the interval's register can record. A coordinator that falls over leaves the seat empty and the shedder does nothing at all until a new election fills it; every ordinary shedding decision goes through the seated coordinator.

The decisions are the obvious ones. The coordinator sheds a served block, which moves it from served to shed. It restores a shed block, which moves it back from shed to served. It commissions a spare block into service, moving it from spare to served. Blocks also come out of service back to spare when a feeder is taken off for maintenance, which is a field operation and does not need the coordinator.

The system operator has an override for the seconds when frequency is falling and there is no coordinator seated: the operator sheds a served block directly. The override is rationed for the interval and each use is written into the disturbance report. It moves a block from served to shed exactly like an ordinary shed does -- what it skips is the coordinator, not the accounting.

The actions of the system are: electing a coordinator and advancing the term, the coordinator falling over and leaving the seat empty, the coordinator shedding a served block, the coordinator restoring a shed block to service, the coordinator commissioning a spare block into service, a feeder being taken off for maintenance so a served block goes back to spare, and the system operator overriding to shed a served block directly.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The blocks being served, the blocks shed and the blocks held in spare always sum to exactly the fixed number of demand blocks in the interval.

       /\ MaxCap \in Nat /\ MaxCap > 0
       /\ MaxGen \in Nat /\ MaxGen > 0

  /\ lobby \subseteq Pax
  /\ riding \in [Cars -> SUBSET Pax]
  /\ delivered \subseteq Pax
  /\ regGen \in 0 .. MaxGen
  /\ notedGen \in [Cars -> 0 .. MaxGen]
  /\ capacity \in 1 .. MaxCap

PassengersArePartitioned ==
  /\ lobby \cup Aboard \cup delivered = Pax
  /\ lobby \cap Aboard = {}
  /\ lobby \cap delivered = {}
  /\ Aboard \cap delivered = {}
  /\ riding[CarOne] \cap riding[CarTwo] = {}

  /\ lobby = Pax
  /\ riding = [c \in Cars |-> {}]
  /\ delivered = {}
  /\ regGen = 0
  /\ notedGen = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ capacity = MaxCap

  /\ notedGen[c] # regGen
  /\ notedGen' = [notedGen EXCEPT ![c] = regGen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, riding, delivered, regGen, capacity>>

  /\ regGen < MaxGen
  /\ p \in lobby
  /\ Cardinality(riding[c]) < capacity

CONSTANTS
    CarOne = elevCarOne
    CarTwo = elevCarTwo
    Pax = {paxA, paxB}
    MaxCap = 2
    MaxGen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PassengersArePartitioned
PROPERTY CarsAlwaysEmpty
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank tracks where every passenger in the system is. A passenger is in exactly one of three places: waiting in the lobby, riding inside exactly one car, or already delivered to a floor. Nobody is ever counted in two places and nobody drops off the roll -- the building's evacuation board is printed off this record, and a passenger who is on it twice or not at all is a passenger the fire service will go looking for in the wrong place.

Boarding is coordinated through a single assignment register that the cars share, using compare-and-swap rather than a lock, because a car cannot afford to wait on a lock while its doors are open. A car reads the register's generation, and boarding only goes ahead if the register is still on that generation when the passenger actually steps in; a successful board advances the generation, which is what makes the other car's read stale. A car whose read has gone stale simply re-reads the register.

Car capacity is not a constant. The building manager retunes it during the day -- a lower figure while a goods move is running and the cars are sharing the shafts with pallets, a higher figure at end of shift. Capacity may be lowered as well as raised, but never below what a car is already carrying, because there is no way to put a passenger back in the lobby out of a moving car. Boarding is only allowed while the boarding car is under its capacity as it stands at that moment.

A car empties at its destination: everybody riding it is delivered in one motion and the car is empty again. Delivered passengers make return trips, coming back into the lobby to wait for another car, which is why the roll never stops moving.

The actions of the system are: a car re-reading the assignment register when its noted generation has gone stale, a car boarding a waiting passenger while its read is current and it is under capacity, which advances the register, a car emptying and delivering everybody riding it, the building manager retuning car capacity to a figure not below what any car is carrying, and a delivered passenger returning to the lobby.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The passengers waiting in the lobby, the passengers riding each car and the passengers already delivered partition the whole set of passengers, with nobody in two places and nobody in none.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A car that has passengers riding it eventually has none, because every car empties at its destination.

CONSTANTS
    Stations = {branchWsA, branchWsB}
    Titles = {titleA, titleB}
    ShelfSize = 2
    Slack = 1
    MaxRev = 2
    NoTitle = noTitle
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ShelvesFitAndDeadStationsHoldNothing
nl:
A public library takes reservations on titles from workstations spread across its branches. Every title has a hold shelf behind the desk, and that shelf has a hard size: the number of copies the library is willing to keep off the open floor waiting for somebody to collect them. Beyond that size the shelf is full and no further hold may be placed on that title.

There is no lock on a title. A workstation opens an attempt against a title, notes the revision that title's hold record was on, and posts the hold only if the record is still on that revision; posting a hold advances the revision, which is what makes every other workstation's noted revision stale. A workstation whose noted revision has gone stale re-reads and works from the new one. A workstation whose title turns out to be full abandons the attempt rather than posting into a full shelf. Cancelling a hold takes a copy back off the shelf and also advances the revision.

Workstations die silently. A branch loses power, a terminal locks up, and the workstation simply stops -- there is no message and no partial write. This is the one place the library gets a free pass: an attempt that has not posted has changed nothing, so a workstation that dies takes its half-finished attempt with it and the hold record is untouched. What the library does insist on is that a dead workstation is never left holding an attempt in the record, because an attempt attributed to a terminal that is not running is an attempt nobody will ever finish or clean up. The branch supervisor brings dead workstations back into service.

The actions of the system are: a workstation opening an attempt against a title and noting its revision, a workstation posting a hold whose noted revision still matches onto a shelf that is under its size, a workstation re-reading a title whose revision moved under its attempt, a workstation abandoning an attempt against a title whose shelf is full, a workstation dying silently and taking its unposted attempt with it, the branch supervisor bringing a dead workstation back into service, and a hold being cancelled off a shelf.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No title's hold shelf ever holds more copies than its size, and no workstation that has died is left holding an attempt in the record.

CONSTANTS
    GangOne = lashGangOne
    GangTwo = lashGangTwo
    SlotCount = 3
    Slack = 1
    MaxShift = 2
    NoGang = noGang
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT StackNeverOverCommitted
PROPERTY GangsAlwaysFinishTheirSet
nl:
A container terminal works its quay stack through lashing gangs, and one gang at a time is the working leader for the berth. The gangs elect a leader and the election stamps a shift number on the winner, up to the highest number the berth log can carry for one shift. A leader that steps down leaves the berth without a leader until the next election; while the berth has no leader, nothing may be reserved.

The quay stack has a hard slot count -- the number of boxes that can stand alongside the crane without fouling the gantry rails. Working the stack goes in two steps. First the leader reserves a slot, which is a promise that a box is on its way and that nobody else may plan into that space. Then a box actually lands in the reserved slot, which converts the reservation into an occupied slot. Boxes also leave the stack when the crane lifts them aboard, freeing a slot outright. The terminal's rule is that reservations and occupied slots together never exceed the slot count, because a reservation that cannot be honoured is a box swinging over a full stack.

Gangs are slow, not absent. A gang that has taken on a piece of work stays on it for a while -- lashing rods do not come off quickly, and there is no way to hurry a gang that is mid-set. What matters is that the gang is still there and will finish; the terminal never has to write a gang off, only wait for it. A gang that is not mid-set can take on a new piece of work at any time.

The actions of the system are: electing a working leader for the berth and advancing the shift number, the leader stepping down and leaving the berth without one, the leader reserving a slot while reservations and occupied slots together are under the slot count, a box landing in a reserved slot and converting it to occupied, the crane lifting a box off the stack and freeing an occupied slot, a gang taking on a piece of work, and a gang finishing the piece of work it was on.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The reserved slots and the occupied slots on the quay stack never together exceed the stack's slot count.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A gang that has taken on a piece of work eventually finishes it and is no longer mid-set.

CONSTANTS
    Units = {surgUnitA, surgUnitB}
    Rooms = {orA, orB, orC}
    Staffed = 2
    MaxGen = 2
    NoRoom = noRoom
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BookingsFitAndApplicableRequestsAreFree
nl:
A hospital books its operating rooms through a single compare-and-swap register that carries a generation number. Requests to book a named room do not reach the register directly: they are posted onto the theatre message bus by the surgical units, and the bus reorders freely. A request that a unit posted first can be processed last, and there is no way for a unit to know where in the order its request will land.

Every posted request carries the room it names and the generation the register was on when the unit posted it. Applying a request is the compare-and-swap: it only takes if the register is still on the generation the request carries, and applying it books the named room and advances the generation. Advancing the generation is what invalidates every other request still sitting on the bus -- their carried generations no longer match, so they are stale and get dropped rather than applied. A unit whose request was dropped posts a fresh one.

The hospital will not staff more than a fixed number of rooms at once, so a request that arrives while that number is already booked is dropped rather than applied, and the unit tries again after a case finishes. Because a request is only ever posted against a room that is free at the moment of posting, and because applying one request makes every other outstanding request stale, no request that is still applicable can be pointing at a room that is already booked.

Cases finishing is a separate ledger operation, not a compare-and-swap: a booked room is released and becomes free again without touching the generation, because releasing a room can only make an outstanding request easier to satisfy, never harder.

The actions of the system are: a unit posting a request naming a room that is free at that moment and carrying the register's current generation, applying a request whose carried generation still matches and booking its room under the staffing number, dropping a request whose carried generation no longer matches, dropping a request that still matches but arrives with the staffing number already reached or the generation book exhausted, and a case finishing and releasing its room.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No more rooms are booked than the hospital staffs, and no request that is still applicable names a room that is already booked.

PROPERTY CorridorAlwaysClears
nl:
A wildfire drone swarm drops retardant through a single descent corridor cut into the smoke column. The corridor takes one aircraft at a time: two drones descending it together in nil visibility is the accident the whole deconfliction scheme exists to prevent. Which drone may use it is decided by a flight director, and the swarm elects one director at a time, the election stamping a rotation number on the winner up to the highest number the sortie log carries.

A director that stands down leaves the swarm without one, and while there is no director nobody may be cleared into the corridor. Directors do not vanish, though -- they go heads-down. A director working a hand-off, or talking to the air attack supervisor on another frequency, is slow rather than absent: it will answer, just not now, and while it is heads-down it cannot issue a clearance or stand down. The swarm never has to write a director off, only wait for one to come back up.

Every drone is either holding above the column or descending the corridor. A director clears exactly one holding drone at a time, and only when the corridor is empty. The cleared drone enters the corridor and switches from holding to descending. When it comes off the bottom of the corridor it goes back to holding, the corridor is empty again, and the clearance is torn up so that the next drone needs a fresh one.

The actions of the system are: electing a flight director and advancing the rotation number, a director standing down and leaving the swarm without one, a director going heads-down, a heads-down director coming back up, a director that is up clearing a holding drone into an empty corridor, the cleared drone entering the corridor and switching to descending, and a descending drone coming off the bottom of the corridor, going back to holding and having its clearance torn up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of drones in the descent corridor is always contained in the set containing just the drone that currently holds a clearance, and every drone in the corridor is in the descending state.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A drone that has entered the descent corridor eventually leaves it.

    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CarLoadsStayUnderTheLimit
PROPERTY InFlightMessagesAlwaysSettle
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator group controller hands hall calls out to cars, and there is a hard limit on how many calls one car may be carrying on its list at a time -- past that limit the car's schedule stops being a schedule and becomes a queue nobody can predict. The limit counts both the calls already on a car's list and the calls that have been dispatched to it but have not landed yet, because a dispatched call is a call the car is going to have to take.

The controller republishes its dispatch plan under a numbered epoch. Every dispatch message carries the epoch the plan was on when the controller sent it. Messages travel over the building's serial loop and arrive out of order: a message sent early can land after one sent later, and there is no sequencing on the loop at all. When the controller republishes -- after a car is taken out for service, after the morning rush profile switches in -- it advances the epoch, and every dispatch message still in flight anywhere on the loop is stale from that instant. A stale message is discarded when it lands rather than being added to any car's list, and the space it was occupying against the limit comes back.

A car works its list by opening its doors at a floor and clearing one call off, then closing them again. Opening and closing doors is the car's own business and has nothing to do with the controller or the loop.

The actions of the system are: the controller republishing the dispatch plan under a new epoch, the controller dispatching a call to a car while that car's list and in-flight messages together are under the limit, a dispatch message landing at a car whose carried epoch is still current and joining that car's list, a stale dispatch message landing at a car and being discarded, a car opening its doors at a floor, a car clearing one call off its list while its doors are open, and a car closing its doors.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every car, the calls on its list plus the dispatch messages in flight to it never together exceed the per-car limit, and no in-flight message carries an epoch ahead of the epoch the controller is currently on.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A car that has dispatch messages in flight to it eventually has none, because every message either lands on its list or is discarded as stale.

CONSTANTS
    Bays = {dispBayA, dispBayB}
    Consoles = {pharmConA, pharmConB, pharmConC}
    MaxOverrides = 1
    NoBay = noBay
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OpenSafeIsGrantedAndJustified
nl:
A hospital pharmacy keeps its narcotics in one safe, and the safe may only be open at one dispensing bay at a time. Two bays with the safe open is not a theft risk so much as a reconciliation impossibility: the count at the end of the shift cannot be attributed and the whole department goes into an audit.

Opening the safe is not one pharmacist's decision. There are several pharmacist consoles, and a bay is only granted the safe once a strict majority of the consoles have approved that bay's request. Approvals accumulate against the bay, and the grant only goes to a bay whose approvals have reached a majority while the safe is not already granted to anyone. Once the grant is in place the bay opens the safe, works, and then closes it -- closing releases the grant, wipes that bay's accumulated approvals, and leaves the safe free for the next bay to be granted.

The chief pharmacist has an override for the case the consoles cannot resolve in time: a patient in theatre needing an infusion now, with one console down and the other two disagreeing. The chief grants a bay the safe directly, without a majority, and the grant is marked as forced so that the morning report can list it. Overrides are rationed for the shift. A forced grant behaves exactly like an ordinary one everywhere else: the bay still has to open the safe, and closing it still releases the grant and clears the mark.

The rule the department is audited against is that every bay with the safe open is the bay the grant is currently sitting with, and that bay either had a majority of console approvals or was forced by the chief. There is no third way to have the safe open.

The actions of the system are: a console approving a bay's request, granting the safe to a bay whose approvals have reached a majority while the safe is ungranted, the chief pharmacist forcing a grant to a bay while the safe is ungranted and overrides remain, a granted bay opening the safe, and a bay closing the safe, releasing the grant, clearing its approvals and clearing any forced mark.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every bay with the safe open is the bay the grant currently sits with, and that bay either holds approvals from a strict majority of consoles or was forced by the chief pharmacist.

  /\ candidate' = c

  /\ v \in {"yes", "no"}

  /\ phase' = "committing"
  /\ pending' = Cranes

  /\ \A c \in Cranes : vote[c] # "none"
  /\ \E c \in Cranes : vote[c] = "no"
  /\ phase' = "aborting"
  /\ pending' = Cranes

  /\ c \in pending

  /\ phase' = IF pending = {c} THEN "idle" ELSE phase

  /\ holder = c
  /\ using = {}
  /\ using' = {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, vote, candidate, holder, pending>>

Unrig(c) ==

  /\ using' = {}
  /\ holder' = NoCrane
  /\ phase' = "idle"

CONSTANTS
    CraneOne = quayCraneOne
    CraneTwo = quayCraneTwo
    NoCrane = noCrane
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BarIsUsedOnlyUnderAGrant
PROPERTY BarUseAlwaysEnds
nl:
A container terminal has two quay cranes and one twin-lift spreader bar between them. The bar bolts onto a crane's headblock and lets it take two forty-foot boxes in a single lift; with two cranes rigged to it at once you get a spreader that is bolted to two moving headblocks, which is how gantries get pulled off their rails. Exactly one crane may be using the bar at a time.

Handing the bar over is run as a two-phase commit. The berth controller opens a round naming one crane as the candidate, and asks both cranes to vote. A crane votes yes if it can free the bar or does not need it, and no if it is mid-lift and cannot. Once both have voted the controller decides -- commit if both said yes, abort otherwise -- and puts a decision message out to each crane.

Those messages go over the terminal's radio link, which reorders them. The crane on the far end of the berth routinely hears before the crane standing next to the controller, and nothing in the protocol assumes otherwise. The round is over when the last decision message has landed. A committed round leaves the bar granted to the candidate crane; an aborted round leaves the bar granted to nobody and the controller free to open another round.

A crane that has been granted the bar rigs it and starts using it. When it finishes it unrigs, which releases the grant and puts the berth back to having no round open and no crane holding the bar.

The actions of the system are: the berth controller opening a round naming a candidate crane and clearing both votes, a crane voting yes, a crane voting no, the controller deciding to commit once both cranes have voted yes, the controller deciding to abort when some crane voted no, a crane receiving a commit decision, a crane receiving an abort decision, a crane that holds the grant rigging the bar and starting to use it, and a crane unrigging the bar and releasing the grant.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of cranes using the spreader bar is always contained in the set containing just the crane the bar is granted to, and a crane is only ever using the bar while the berth is in the granted state.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A crane that has started using the spreader bar eventually stops using it.

CONSTANTS
    Sessions = {memberSessA, memberSessB}
    Levels = {priceLvlA, priceLvlB}
    Depth = 2
    Slack = 1
    NoSession = noSession
    NoLevel = noLevel
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DepthLimitIsRespected
nl:
The opening auction on a stock exchange collects resting orders at a set of price levels, and every level has a hard depth limit -- the number of orders the matching engine will hold at that price before it refuses more. The limit counts orders already resting at the level and orders that have been submitted for it but have not been written in yet, because a submitted order is depth that is coming.

Member sessions reach the book through two levels of lock, taken in a fixed order. A session first takes the book lock, which the whole auction shares and which only one session can hold. Only then may it take the lock on the particular price level it wants to work, and only then may it submit an order for that level. Releasing gives up the level lock and the book lock together. The ordering is not decoration: sessions that grabbed level locks directly used to deadlock against each other across two levels during the pre-open.

Submitted orders do not reach the book immediately. They go onto the entry bus, which reorders freely: an order submitted for one level can be written into the book long after one submitted later for another level, and the engine writes whatever is at the front of whichever queue it services next. That is why the depth limit has to count the orders still on the bus -- checking only what is resting would let a session submit into a level that is about to fill up from the bus.

Orders are also cancelled off levels, which frees depth outright and does not go through the bus at all.

The actions of the system are: a session taking the book lock, a session that holds the book lock taking a free price level's lock, a session submitting an order for the level it holds while that level's resting orders and bussed orders together are under the depth limit, the engine writing one bussed order into the level it was submitted for, a resting order being cancelled off a level, and a session releasing its level lock and the book lock together.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every price level, the orders resting at it plus the orders still on the entry bus for it never together exceed that level's depth limit.

CONSTANTS
    MachOne = stackerOne
    MachTwo = stackerTwo
    MaxTier = 2
    MaxGen = 2
    Nobody = nobodyHolds
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LaneIsExclusiveAndStackIsLegal
PROPERTY LaneIsAlwaysVacated
nl:
A container yard has one reach-stacker lane running between the blocks, wide enough for exactly one machine. Two machines in the lane at once is a wedge that stops the whole block until somebody reverses one of them out by hand, so the lane is held by one machine at a time and no machine may enter it without holding it.

The lane is arbitrated by a single compare-and-swap register rather than a lock, because the machines' radios drop out often enough that a lock holder that went off air would strand the lane. The register carries a generation number and the name of the machine that holds the lane, or nobody. A machine takes the lane by reading the register, finding it free, and swapping in its own name; the swap only takes if the generation has not moved since the read, and taking it advances the generation. A machine whose read has gone stale re-reads and tries again. Giving the lane back swaps the register back to nobody and also advances the generation.

The yard's stacking height is retuned during the day. Wind limits, the block's ground bearing after rain, and whether the reefer racks are in the way all change how many tiers the yard master will allow, and the figure moves up and down during a shift. It may never be set below the tiers already stacked, because there is no way to unstack a block instantly. A machine in the lane only adds a tier while the stack is under the allowance as it stands at that moment; tiers also come off when boxes are picked.

The actions of the system are: a machine re-reading the register when its noted generation has gone stale, a machine taking the free lane by compare-and-swap and advancing the generation, a machine that holds the lane entering it, a machine leaving the lane and swapping the register back to nobody, a machine in the lane adding a tier while the stack is under the allowance, a box being picked so a tier comes off, and the yard master retuning the tier allowance to a figure not below what is already stacked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of machines in the reach-stacker lane is always contained in the set containing just the machine the register names as the lane holder, and the stack is never higher than the tier allowance currently in force.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A machine that has entered the lane eventually leaves it.

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {allocNodeA, allocNodeB}
    Slots = {slotA, slotB}
    MaxPeriod = 2
    NoNode = noNode
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SlotBookIsPartitioned
nl:
An air-traffic facility allocates arrival slots for a runway out of a fixed slot book. The book is fixed for the period: the facility does not invent slots and does not lose them. Every slot in the book is in exactly one of three states at any instant -- free in the book, allocated to an inbound flight, or already flown. Nothing else is a state a slot can be in, and no slot is ever in two of them.

Allocation is done by whichever node currently holds the allocator seat. The nodes elect one, and the election stamps a period number on the winner up to the highest the facility's log will carry. Only a seated allocator may take a slot out of the free book and allocate it. Everything else -- a flight releasing a slot it will not use, a flight actually landing, the overnight rebuild that returns flown slots to the free book for the next period -- happens without the seat, because those are field events rather than allocation decisions.

Allocator nodes fail silently. A node stops answering with no alarm and no handover; the facility only finds out because allocations stop happening. A node that has failed cannot be elected until the technical staff bring it back up, and while the seat is empty no new slot is allocated at all. Slots already allocated are unaffected: a silent failure of the allocator does not un-allocate anybody's slot, which is exactly why the failure is survivable.

The actions of the system are: electing an allocator and advancing the period number, the seated allocator failing silently and leaving the seat empty, the seated allocator allocating a free slot to an inbound flight, a flight releasing an allocated slot back to the free book, a flight flying an allocated slot, the overnight rebuild returning a flown slot to the free book, and the technical staff bringing a failed node back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The free slots, the allocated slots and the flown slots partition the whole slot book, with no slot in two of those states and none in fewer than one.

CONSTANTS
    Staff = {bankStaffA, bankStaffB}
    Fridges = {fridgeA, fridgeB}
    MaxSlots = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoFridge = noFridge
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT WorkIsBadgedAndFridgesFit
nl:
A blood bank stores units in a bank of fridges, and every fridge has a slot count -- how many units it will hold at the temperature the standard requires. Staff work at a fridge under a credential, and the bank republishes its credential set under a numbered epoch whenever the roster changes, a competency review lands, or an incident closes. Republishing advances the epoch and, in the same motion, ends every piece of work anybody had open at any fridge, because the credentials those staff were working under are no longer the credentials in force.

A member of staff whose badge is behind the current epoch is stale and may not open work at a fridge. Re-badging brings a badge up to the epoch in force, and only then may that member of staff start work. The bank is strict about it because a unit stored or issued under a credential that has been withdrawn has to be quarantined and re-tested, and the fridge it sat in has to be logged as suspect.

The slot count is retuned during the day. Slots are given over to platelets when a theatre list needs them and taken back for red cells afterwards, so a fridge's count moves both ways. It may never be set below what the fridge is already holding, because there is nowhere for displaced units to go and moving stock between fridges is a separate, audited operation. A member of staff at a fridge may store a unit only while that fridge is under its count as it stands at that moment, and may issue a unit off it at any time.

The actions of the system are: republishing the credential set under a new epoch and ending every piece of open work, a member of staff re-badging to the epoch in force, a currently badged member of staff opening work at a fridge, a member of staff storing a unit into their fridge while it is under its slot count, a member of staff issuing a unit off their fridge, a member of staff closing their own work, and the bank retuning a fridge's slot count to any value not below what that fridge is already holding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every member of staff with work open at a fridge holds a badge stamped with the epoch currently in force, and no fridge ever holds more units than its current slot count.

CONSTANTS
    OpOne = routerOpOne
    OpTwo = routerOpTwo
    Bags = {bagA, bagB}
    Ceiling = 2
    NoBag = noBag
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DisposalsHappenAtMostOnce
PROPERTY RequestsAlwaysSettle
nl:
An airport baggage router has a disposal chute for bags that have gone through the whole unclaimed-baggage process and are to be destroyed. Sending a bag down that chute is irreversible: there is no path back, and a bag that goes down it twice is a bag whose paperwork says one thing and whose count says another. Each bag may therefore be sent down the chute at most once.

The router does not lock bag records. An operator opens a disposal request against a bag and notes the status version that bag's record was on. The request then goes onto the router's control bus, and the bus reorders freely -- a request raised early can be acted on last, and there is no ordering between the requests of different operators at all. Acting on a request is only allowed if the bag's status version is still the one the request noted; anything else has happened to that bag since, and the request is stale and is dropped rather than acted on.

Every event that touches a bag's record advances its status version: a disposal, a re-scan when the bag turns up on a different belt, and an owner claim being registered. Advancing the version is exactly what makes every other request outstanding against that bag stale, and it is the mechanism that stops two operators both disposing of the same bag: whichever request is acted on first advances the version and invalidates the rest.

Bags stop accepting record events once they reach the version ceiling the router keeps for one operating day; an operator holding a request against a bag at the ceiling drops it rather than retrying.

The actions of the system are: an operator opening a disposal request against a bag and noting its status version, an operator acting on a request whose noted version still matches and sending that bag down the chute, an operator dropping a request whose noted version no longer matches, an operator dropping a request against a bag that has reached the day's version ceiling, a bag being re-scanned onto a different belt, and an owner claim being registered against a bag, which marks it claimed and puts it permanently out of reach of the chute.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No bag has been sent down the disposal chute more than once, no outstanding request was noted against a status version ahead of the one its bag is actually on, and no bag with an owner claim registered against it has ever been sent down the chute.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: An operator holding an outstanding disposal request eventually holds none, whether it is acted on or dropped.

  /\ r \notin moving

CONSTANTS
    BotOne = aisleBotOne
    BotTwo = aisleBotTwo
    MaxGen = 2
    LeaseLen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MovingRobotsHoldCurrentLiveLeases
PROPERTY MovingRobotsAlwaysStop
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet works the aisles under leases. A robot may only be under power and moving while it holds a live lease, and every lease is stamped with the fleet configuration generation that was in force when it was granted. The configuration generation changes whenever the aisle map is redrawn -- a rack bay is pulled out, a one-way aisle is reversed, a charging bank is relocated. Redrawing advances the generation and, in the same motion, stops every robot that is moving, because a robot running a route computed against the old map is a robot heading for a rack that is no longer where it thinks it is.

A lease stamped with an older generation is stale, and a robot holding a stale lease is not a robot the fleet controller will let move. Leases are never renewed in place: a robot with a stale or expired lease has to be granted a fresh one, stamped with the generation currently in force, before it may start moving again.

Every lease carries a countdown. The countdown runs down step by step while the lease is live, and when it reaches its last step the lease expires and the robot is stopped in the same motion. That is what bounds how long any robot can be out on the floor without the controller reconsidering it, and it is what makes a robot that has stopped answering harmless.

Robots fail silently. A robot's radio drops and it stops reporting with no fault code; the controller finds out only because the robot's telemetry goes flat. A silently failed robot may not be granted a lease and may not start moving. Recovery clears the failure and stops the robot, and it comes back onto the floor by being granted a fresh lease like anybody else.

The actions of the system are: redrawing the aisle map, which advances the configuration generation and stops every moving robot, granting a fresh lease stamped with the current generation to a robot that is not failed and has no countdown left, a robot with a current live lease starting to move, a live lease's countdown running down one step, a lease expiring on its last step and stopping its robot, a robot failing silently, and a failed robot being recovered and stopped.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every robot that is moving holds a lease stamped with the configuration generation currently in force and with countdown still left on it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A robot that is moving eventually stops moving, because every lease countdown runs out.

CONSTANTS
    Cubicles = {pointCub, signalCub, xingCub}
    Generations = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT StagedChangesRestOnTheirOwnGeneration
nl:
Setting a route across a metro junction touches several interlocking cubicles at once -- the point machines, the signal group and the level-crossing controller each hold their own copy of the junction's route table. A route that lands in some cubicles and not others is a route that is set in the signal's opinion and not set in the points', which is the class of fault that closes a railway for a day. Route changes therefore go through a two-phase commit run by the junction controller.

The controller starts a round, numbered so that the cubicles can tell rounds apart. Each cubicle either prepares, which means noting the generation its own route table is on as the basis for the change it has staged, or refuses. Once every cubicle has answered, the controller writes the round's outcome into the decision register: commit if all prepared, abort otherwise.

The cubicles do not have the decision pushed to them. Each one pulls it from the register when its own polling cycle comes round, and those cycles are not synchronised in any way -- the crossing controller polls on a slow loop and routinely pulls minutes after the point machines have already acted. A cubicle only acts on a decision stamped with the round it prepared in; a decision from an older round is not its business. When the controller starts a new round it clears the record of who has pulled, because pulls from the previous round mean nothing to this one.

A cubicle may also edit its own route table between rounds, and only while it has not prepared. That restriction is the point: a prepared cubicle has a change resting on a noted generation, and if it moved its own generation underneath that staged change, committing it later would silently discard whatever moved it.

The actions of the system are: the controller starting a numbered round and clearing every answer and every record of who has pulled, a cubicle preparing and noting its route table's current generation, a cubicle refusing, the controller writing a commit outcome once every cubicle has prepared, the controller writing an abort outcome when some cubicle refused, a cubicle pulling a commit outcome and advancing its own generation, a cubicle pulling an abort outcome and discarding its staged change, and a cubicle editing its own route table between rounds.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every prepared cubicle has its staged change resting on exactly the generation its own route table is currently on, and no cubicle is recorded as having pulled this round's outcome while the controller is still collecting answers.

CONSTANTS

    SiteClinic = siteClinic

SPECIFICATION Spec

PROPERTY SettlingAlwaysCompletes
nl:
A blood bank's inventory record is mirrored at several sites -- the main laboratory, the theatre satellite fridge and the remote clinic -- and a change to a unit's record has to land at all of them or none. A change that lands at two of three leaves the clinic issuing a unit the laboratory has already crossmatched to somebody else. Changes therefore go through a two-phase commit run by the bank's coordinator.

The coordinator opens a round and asks every site to prepare. A site that prepares notes the generation its own copy of the record is on, and that noted generation is the basis of the change it has staged. A site that cannot take the change refuses. Once every site has answered the coordinator decides: commit if all prepared, abort otherwise. A site that receives a commit applies the change and advances its own generation; a site that receives an abort discards its staged change. Either way the site goes back to having no answer outstanding.

Sites here are slow, not broken. The remote clinic is on a link that comes and goes, and the theatre satellite is behind a firewall that batches traffic; when a round opens, a site cannot answer straight away. Each site works through its own settling delay first, and only once that delay has run out is it able to prepare or refuse. Nothing writes a slow site off and no timeout fires against it -- the round simply waits, because the bank would rather hold a round open than commit a record change without the clinic in it.

A site may edit its own copy only between rounds and only while it has no answer outstanding. A site that has prepared has a change resting on a noted generation, and moving its own generation underneath that staged change would silently discard whatever moved it.

The actions of the system are: the coordinator opening a round, clearing every answer and winding each site's settling delay, a site working one step through its settling delay, a settled site preparing and noting its record generation, a settled site refusing, the coordinator deciding to commit once every site has prepared, the coordinator deciding to abort when some site refused, a site applying a commit and advancing its generation, a site discarding its staged change on an abort, and a site editing its own copy between rounds.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every site that has prepared has its staged change resting on exactly the generation its own copy is currently on, and no site has prepared before its settling delay ran out.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A site that still has settling delay left eventually has none, because the delay always runs down.

---- MODULE W4Od15m8p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Firms, MaxSlots, NoFirm, NoSlot

SlotNums == 1 .. MaxSlots

ASSUME /\ NoFirm \notin Firms
       /\ MaxSlots \in Nat /\ MaxSlots > 0

VARIABLES bandLock, slotLock, holding, allocation, openSlots

vars == <<bandLock, slotLock, holding, allocation, openSlots>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ bandLock \in Firms \cup {NoFirm}
  /\ slotLock \in [SlotNums -> Firms \cup {NoFirm}]
  /\ holding \in [Firms -> SlotNums \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ allocation \in [SlotNums -> Firms \cup {NoFirm}]
  /\ openSlots \in 1 .. MaxSlots

Placed == {f \in Firms : holding[f] # NoSlot /\ allocation[holding[f]] = f}

AllocationsAreSingleAndInRange ==
  /\ \A f \in Placed : slotLock[holding[f]] = f /\ bandLock = f
  /\ \A n \in SlotNums : allocation[n] # NoFirm => n <= openSlots

Init ==
  /\ bandLock = NoFirm
  /\ slotLock = [n \in SlotNums |-> NoFirm]
  /\ holding = [f \in Firms |-> NoSlot]
  /\ allocation = [n \in SlotNums |-> NoFirm]
  /\ openSlots = MaxSlots

TakeBandLock(f) ==
  /\ bandLock = NoFirm
  /\ bandLock' = f
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, holding, allocation, openSlots>>

TakeSlotLock(f, n) ==
  /\ bandLock = f
  /\ holding[f] = NoSlot
  /\ n <= openSlots
  /\ slotLock[n] = NoFirm
  /\ allocation[n] = NoFirm
  /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![n] = f]
  /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![f] = n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bandLock, allocation, openSlots>>

WriteAllocation(f) ==
  /\ bandLock = f
  /\ holding[f] # NoSlot
  /\ slotLock[holding[f]] = f
  /\ allocation[holding[f]] = NoFirm
  /\ holding[f] <= openSlots
  /\ allocation' = [allocation EXCEPT ![holding[f]] = f]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bandLock, slotLock, holding, openSlots>>

GiveUpSlot(f) ==
  /\ holding[f] # NoSlot
  /\ allocation' = [allocation EXCEPT ![holding[f]] = NoFirm]
  /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![holding[f]] = NoFirm]
  /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]
  /\ bandLock' = IF bandLock = f THEN NoFirm ELSE bandLock
  /\ UNCHANGED openSlots

RetuneOpenSlots(k) ==
  /\ k \in 1 .. MaxSlots
  /\ \A n \in SlotNums : allocation[n] # NoFirm => n <= k
  /\ openSlots' = k
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bandLock, slotLock, holding, allocation>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in 1 .. MaxSlots : RetuneOpenSlots(k)
  \/ \E f \in Firms :
       \/ TakeBandLock(f) \/ WriteAllocation(f) \/ GiveUpSlot(f)
       \/ \E n \in SlotNums : TakeSlotLock(f, n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Firms = {mmFirmA, mmFirmB}
    MaxSlots = 3
    NoFirm = noFirm
    NoSlot = 0
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AllocationsAreSingleAndInRange
nl:
A stock exchange sells market-maker quote slots in a price band. The slots are numbered, and a slot is allocated to at most one firm: two firms quoting the same slot puts two obligations on one line in the obligations file and the surveillance team cannot tell whose quote is whose.

Getting a slot goes through two levels of lock, taken in a fixed order. A firm takes the band lock first -- one firm at a time holds it for the whole band -- and only then may it take the lock on the particular numbered slot it wants. Nobody may take a slot lock without already holding the band lock, and that ordering is what stopped the deadlocks the exchange used to see when firms grabbed slot locks directly during the open. A firm that holds both locks writes itself into that slot's allocation. Giving the slot up clears the allocation, drops the slot lock and drops the band lock together.

How many slots the band actually offers is retuned during the session. The exchange opens more slots when the book thickens and pulls them back when a symbol is put into an auction, and the figure moves both ways. It may never be set below the highest-numbered slot that is currently allocated, because there is no mechanism to move a firm's obligations down into a lower-numbered slot, and no slot above the current figure may be locked or allocated at all.

The actions of the system are: a firm taking the band lock, a firm that holds the band lock taking the lock on a free, unallocated slot within the number of slots currently open, a firm that holds a slot lock writing itself into that slot's allocation, a firm giving the slot up and dropping both locks together, and the exchange retuning the number of open slots to any figure not below the highest-numbered allocated slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every firm that has been written into a slot is the firm that slot's allocation names, so no slot is ever allocated to two firms, and no allocated slot is numbered above the number of slots the band currently offers.

---- MODULE W4Od16m1p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS RingSize, StockedUnits

ASSUME RingSize \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME StockedUnits \in Nat

Lines == 0 .. RingSize - 1

VARIABLES vault, trolley, drawer, given, token

vars == <<vault, trolley, drawer, given, token>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ vault \in 0 .. StockedUnits
    /\ trolley \in [Lines -> 0 .. StockedUnits]
    /\ drawer \in [Lines -> 0 .. StockedUnits]
    /\ given \in 0 .. StockedUnits
    /\ token \in Lines

Init ==
    /\ vault = StockedUnits
    /\ trolley = [l \in Lines |-> 0]
    /\ drawer = [l \in Lines |-> 0]
    /\ given = 0
    /\ token = 0

\* Only the token holder may open the vault; everything below the vault is
\* local to a line and needs no arbitration.
Draw(l) ==
    /\ token = l
    /\ vault > 0
    /\ vault' = vault - 1
    /\ trolley' = [trolley EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drawer, given, token>>

Deliver(l) ==
    /\ trolley[l] > 0
    /\ trolley' = [trolley EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
    /\ drawer' = [drawer EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, given, token>>

Administer(l) ==
    /\ drawer[l] > 0
    /\ drawer' = [drawer EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
    /\ given' = given + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, trolley, token>>

\* Stock also flows back up, which is where a bookkeeping slip is easiest.
Return(l) ==
    /\ drawer[l] > 0
    /\ drawer' = [drawer EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
    /\ vault' = vault + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<trolley, given, token>>

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % RingSize
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, trolley, drawer, given>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Lines : Draw(l)
    \/ \E l \in Lines : Deliver(l)
    \/ \E l \in Lines : Administer(l)
    \/ \E l \in Lines : Return(l)
    \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every ampoule is in exactly one place, so the four places plus the
\* administered tally must always add back up to what was stocked.
UnitsAreConserved ==
    vault + SumOver(trolley, Lines) + SumOver(drawer, Lines) + given
        = StockedUnits

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 2
    StockedUnits = 4

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT UnitsAreConserved
nl:
A hospital pharmacy holds a controlled drug in a single vault and feeds two dispensing lines from it: the inpatient line and the outpatient line. The two lines are run by separate teams on separate schedules and neither knows what the other is doing; what they share is the one vault. The quantity that matters here is countable physical stock -- ampoules -- and the whole point of the paperwork around a controlled drug is that the count never drifts. An ampoule is at any moment in exactly one place: still in the vault, on the trolley in transit to a line, sitting in a line's local drawer, or already administered to a patient.

Access to the vault is arbitrated by a work token that circulates around the lines in a fixed ring. Only the line currently holding the token may draw stock out of the vault. The token moves on unconditionally, so neither line can monopolise the vault and neither can stall the other.

Everything downstream of the vault draw is local to a line and needs no token: the trolley arriving at a line, a drawer ampoule being administered, and a drawer ampoule being walked back and returned to the vault all happen on the line's own initiative. Returns are what make this more than a one-way flow -- stock can move back up as well as down, and a bookkeeping slip on the way back is as damaging as one on the way out.

The full set of actions is: Draw, in which the line currently holding the token takes one ampoule out of the vault and onto its trolley, provided the vault is not empty; Deliver, in which one ampoule on a line's trolley arrives in that line's drawer; Administer, in which one ampoule in a line's drawer is given to a patient and leaves circulation; Return, in which one ampoule in a line's drawer is walked back and put into the vault; and PassToken, in which the work token moves to the next line in the ring.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of ampoules is conserved -- the count in the vault, plus the counts on both lines' trolleys, plus the counts in both lines' drawers, plus the count already administered, always equals the quantity the vault was stocked with, so no movement of stock ever creates or destroys an ampoule.

---- MODULE W4Od10m1p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Interlockings, Sections, NoOne

ASSUME NoOne \notin Interlockings

VARIABLES pool, held, occupied, authorisedBy, token

vars == <<pool, held, occupied, authorisedBy, token>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in SUBSET Sections
    /\ held \in [Interlockings -> SUBSET Sections]
    /\ occupied \in SUBSET Sections
    /\ authorisedBy \in [Sections -> Interlockings \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ token \in Interlockings

Init ==
    /\ pool = Sections
    /\ held = [i \in Interlockings |-> {}]
    /\ occupied = {}
    /\ authorisedBy = [s \in Sections |-> NoOne]
    /\ token = CHOOSE i \in Interlockings : TRUE

Released == {s \in Sections : authorisedBy[s] # NoOne}
InHand == UNION {held[i] : i \in Interlockings}

\* A permit only leaves the shared pool into the hands of the token holder.
TakePermit(i, s) ==
    /\ token = i
    /\ s \in pool
    /\ pool' = pool \ {s}
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, authorisedBy, token>>

Yield(i, s) ==
    /\ s \in held[i]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, authorisedBy, token>>

\* Spending a permit consumes it: it is not returned to the pool, and no
\* later action mints another, so the release cannot be repeated.
Release(i, s) ==
    /\ s \in held[i]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {s}
    /\ authorisedBy' = [authorisedBy EXCEPT ![s] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, token>>

Traverse(s) ==
    /\ s \in occupied
    /\ occupied' = occupied \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, authorisedBy, token>>

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = CHOOSE j \in Interlockings : j # token
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, occupied, authorisedBy>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Interlockings, s \in Sections : TakePermit(i, s)
    \/ \E i \in Interlockings, s \in Sections : Yield(i, s)
    \/ \E i \in Interlockings, s \in Sections : Release(i, s)
    \/ \E s \in Sections : Traverse(s)
    \/ PassToken

\* Taking is always available while the pool is non-empty, so weak fairness
\* carries it; releasing competes with yielding, so it needs strong fairness.
Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(PassToken)
    /\ WF_vars(\E i \in Interlockings, s \in Sections : TakePermit(i, s))
    /\ SF_vars(\E i \in Interlockings, s \in Sections : Release(i, s))

\* A released section's permit is gone from everywhere it could be reused.
PermitsAreSpentOnce == Released \cap (pool \cup InHand) = {}

\* No section's authority is left circulating forever.
EverySectionEventuallyRuns == <>(Released = Sections)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Interlockings = {north, south}
    Sections = {blkA, blkB, blkC}
    NoOne = none

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT PermitsAreSpentOnce

PROPERTY EverySectionEventuallyRuns
nl:
A metro network has a pool of single-track block sections that two signalling instances -- the north interlocking and the south interlocking -- both draw from. The two instances are independent: they were commissioned separately, run their own timetables, and do not talk to each other. What they share is the one pool of sections and one movement authority per section.

Releasing a train into a block section is the irreversible act here. A movement authority for a section exists exactly once, as a physical permit. An interlocking may only pick up a permit from the shared pool while the control token is with it; the token circulates around the two interlockings in a ring. Once an interlocking has a permit it may hold it, hand it back to the pool if it has no train to run, or spend it by releasing a train into that section. Spending the permit consumes it: the permit does not go back into the pool and there is no way to manufacture another, which is what makes the release irreversible and unrepeatable. A train that has been released into a section later traverses it and the section is reported clear, but clearing a section does not mint a new permit for it -- the timetable's authority for that section has been used up.

Because both interlockings draw from the one pool, the whole danger is a permit for a section that has already been released finding its way back into circulation and a second train being sent into an occupied or already-used block.

The full set of actions is: TakePermit, in which the interlocking currently holding the control token picks up a permit for some section out of the shared pool; Yield, in which an interlocking puts a permit it holds back into the shared pool without using it; Release, in which an interlocking spends a permit it holds, sending a train into that section, recording which interlocking authorised it, marking the section occupied, and consuming the permit entirely; Traverse, in which a train leaves a section it occupies and the section is reported clear without any permit being minted; and PassToken, in which the control token moves to the other interlocking in the ring.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A section that has been released to a train has no permit anywhere in the system -- the set of released sections is disjoint from the shared pool and from both interlockings' held permits -- so the irreversible release of a section can never happen a second time.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every block section is eventually released to a train, so no section's movement authority sits in the pool or in an interlocking's hand forever while the timetable stalls.
